sections.h2: Ways to sell in Hurst, TX
sections.html:
An owner in Hurst can go with an agent, sell without one, or accept a direct cash purchase. Which fits depends on how much the house needs, what you still owe and when you need to be done.

Hurst is a compact suburb in the northeast corner of Tarrant County, north of Fort Worth near State Highways 121 and 10. The city has almost no raw land left, so almost every sale here is a resale of a house with some years on it. Owners who stage well do fine. Others face a roof, slab or kitchen that would cost more to fix than a listing would bring back, and a direct sale suits them.

  • Agent: the most eyes on the house, paid for with showings and a repair list after the buyer's inspector visits.
  • On your own: no listing commission, yet every contract and title form lands on your desk.
  • Cash buyer: fewer moving parts and a shorter path, with the house taken as it stands.

sections.h2: Why so many Hurst houses are from the postwar years
sections.html:
In the years after 1951, the town boomed. After Bell Aircraft announced a helicopter plant in 1951, residents voted 36 to 24 to incorporate. North East Mall opened in 1972, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport in January 1974, and the population was above 27,200 by 1970.

That boom explains why many Hurst houses are fifty to seventy years old. Older houses can carry original wiring, plumbing and slab issues, and buyers will price those in. The city footprint has barely changed since, so you are selling in a mature neighborhood with established trees and close access to employers on both sides of the Trinity River.

Hurst, Euless and Bedford share a school district. Put the district and the closest highways in your listing text. Shoppers filter on both.

Before you list, call the City of Hurst to confirm that any permits for completed work, such as a remodel or a fence, were closed out. An open permit is the kind of loose end that makes an underwriter hesitate.

sections.h2: Which office bills a Hurst homeowner?
sections.html:
Hurst sits in Tarrant County, so the county Tax Assessor-Collector handles collection. Its address is 100 E. Weatherford Street in Fort Worth, the number is 817-884-1100, and eight branch offices handle walk-in payments.

The county tax page offers a property tax estimator, a list of important tax dates and delinquent tax sale information. A truth-in-taxation database shows what each taxing unit has proposed for a given parcel. A bill is a stack of separate charges from the city, the county and the school district, so read each line on its own.

Anything unpaid after January 31 is delinquent from the next day. The charges stack up like this.

Late-payment charges on Texas property tax bills
TimingCharge
February 1A six percent penalty starts, with one percent interest
March through JuneEach month adds another percent of penalty and another percent of interest
July 1Penalty reaches its 12 percent level
Attorney collectionUp to 20 percent more on top

Interest has no ceiling. The January lien can be enforced against the house even after it changes hands, which is why a buyer's title company cares about your unpaid tax as much as you do.

sections.h2: What if I am facing foreclosure on a Hurst house?
sections.html:
Texas lenders seldom go to court. They rely on the power of sale written into the deed of trust, and the timeline moves in fixed steps.

  • First comes a default letter and a brief chance to catch up.
  • Then a sale notice goes up at the courthouse and into the clerk's files, three weeks before the auction.
  • Auctions fall on a first Tuesday, and for a Hurst house the sale is held in Tarrant County.

A servicer is normally barred by federal rules from starting until the loan is well beyond four months late. Closing a sale first can save equity and your credit. Weigh that against your other choices, and talk to a housing counselor or attorney.

The Tarrant County clerk files Hurst deeds and can quote the records charges for yours.

Homestead owners get a $140,000 school deduction and a ten percent yearly cap on appraisal growth, and seniors and disabled owners get an additional $60,000 for school taxes. Mention your exemption status in the sale materials so a lender can estimate the buyer's monthly cost.

The law separates tenants from squatters. A tenant is owed a written notice to vacate, and if the tenant stays, the landlord files in justice court. Someone who moved in with no right whatsoever falls under Property Code chapter 24B, so the owner can ask the sheriff or constable to remove them. That route is closed when the occupant is family or a past or present tenant, or when a suit is pending.

  • A hearing is set within a few weeks after the suit is filed.
  • Only a final judgment brings a writ of possession.
  • Removing someone wrongly can bring a lawsuit against the owner.

Before you file any removal request, talk it over with a Tarrant County attorney. Keeping an empty house locked, checked and insured is the simplest protection while it sits.

sections.h2: Preparing a Hurst house for a quick closing
sections.html: A cash buyer in Hurst can often promise a closing within weeks. Someone financing with a mortgage needs an appraisal and underwriting first, and that stretches the calendar. Either way, decide before the first showing whether you will repair, sell as-is or price for someone who plans to renovate. Houses built in the postwar decades often draw buyers who expect to update the kitchen, wiring or plumbing, so a fair as-is price can find a taker quickly. Before signing with anyone, request proof of funds or a lender letter, and get in writing who pays for the title policy and recording.

sections.h2: A step-by-step path from decision to closing
sections.html:
Step one is choosing the route. Listing means showings, an inspection, repair requests and then a lender's schedule. Selling alone hands you the contract and title forms. Cash usually skips the repairs and moves faster. For most Hurst sellers the deciding question is how many weeks they can afford to wait.

Step two is paperwork: the deed, a payoff letter when a loan exists and the newest Tarrant County tax statement. Have the title company check for liens or unfinished permits. Step three is a side-by-side look at the written offers, comparing dates, closing costs and each buyer's reaction to inspection findings.

Step four is the signing. A notary must be present so the deed can go to the county clerk, and the recorded copy belongs in your files.

Back taxes do not require cash up front. At closing the agent can settle the balance out of your proceeds, because the title company wants that lien gone before it insures the new owner. Get a current statement from the Tarrant County tax office early. On a homestead, ask whether an installment arrangement fits before the penalty reaches 12 percent in July. Selling ahead of that step often costs less than waiting for it.

faqs.a: Tarrant County. Hurst is in the northeastern quadrant, just north of Fort Worth.

faqs.q: Who handles a Hurst tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tarrant County Tax Assessor-Collector, reachable at 817-884-1100 or at the Fort Worth office on East Weatherford Street.
Yes, if the sale closes before the auction and pays off the loan. Auctions come monthly, so begin early.

faqs.q: When does a Texas tax bill go late?
faqs.a: Once January 31 passes in most cases, with penalty and interest running from February 1.

faqs.q: Must I hire a lawyer to sell in Hurst?
faqs.a: The state does not require it. A lien, a probate matter or a foreclosure notice is still worth a lawyer's time.
